# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (seed→child) — teach the prompt the benchmark mechanics: general re-run code, inspect-real-layout, verify output, formulas-OK
- Changes I made (prompt.md only — system-prompt is the sole editable artifact; no tools.py exists):
  1. New "Write GENERAL code" section — code is re-run on 3 hidden files (same layout, diff data/size); discover rows/cols dynamically, MATCH source→dest by header/label/key not position, never hardcode preview positions/counts/values. Targets flaky cluster (52216/374-9/53161/160-6) + 347-49 hardcoding.
  2. New "INSPECT real file first" + literal A1-mapping worked examples; warns the pandas preview mislabels headers (first data row shown as header). Targets 347-49 offset + placement class.
  3. New "VERIFY before finish" step — re-open saved file, print answer_position, fix if empty/wrong; explicit note openpyxl showing formula text is expected (guards 40467). Targets None/misplaced cells across all failing tasks.
  4. Rewrote misleading "prefer LITERAL values over formulas" → "both acceptable, grader recalcs; make formulas relative/full-extent."
- Expected effect + why safe: all four are ADDITIVE knowledge/clarifications, no ACT-vs-REFUSE rule touched. Passing tasks 47484/418-29/40467 re-checked against their final code — each already inspects via openpyxl, generalizes dynamically, and places values correctly; 40467 keeps its live formulas (encouraged). None of the edits flips their action → bounded, no regression by construction.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — this is the seed's first child (LEDGER/RUNMAP empty).
- Refuted hypotheses (proven in-analysis, never re-test): "grader does not evaluate formulas / avoid formulas" is FALSE — 40467 passes 5/5 writing live formulas; the grader recalcs. Do NOT add any anti-formula rule; it regresses 40467.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 32468 (12-month SUMIFS domain logic) and 347-49 (exact blank-rows-to-delete) are reasoning gaps a general prompt rule can't encode without hardcoding the answer; 55457 has an EMPTY instruction (non-breaking space) — not prompt-fixable, do not chase it.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first child). If this is rejected as net-zero, the lever to try next is a compact worked `<example>` of the full inspect→map→verify loop, or narrowing the generalization rule further — NOT re-touching formulas.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, push on the flaky tasks' remaining variance (52216 case3, 53161) with a sharper match-by-key example; leave 55457 alone.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.453 Δ=-0.053 · fixed={160-6} · broke={418-29}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

## Iteration cand_0002 (seed→child) — surgical ADDITIVE prompt rules; keep seed verbatim, avoid cand_0001's header-distrust hazard
- Changes I made (prompt.md only; the seed's original 6 bullets kept verbatim, 6 new sections appended):
  1. Output contract: "reply with exactly ONE ```python block; never emit `<function_calls>/<invoke>/<parameter>` XML — it doesn't execute and wastes the round." Targets the round-wasting XML glitch seen in EVERY failing/flaky trial.
  2. Inspect-before-solve (when unsure): confirm each table's location, orientation (matrix vs records), true extent; match cross-table pulls by label not position. Targets 53161 t1/t3 + 160-6 t3 (fabricated layouts). NO header-distrust claim.
  3. "Apply all/every conditions across the whole region; a label/subtotal between match-groups must not stop the scan; example numbers are illustrative." Targets 347-49 (0.00).
  4. "answer_position bounds WRITES, not READS — source may lie outside it; compute post-op contents then write; fill EVERY target cell." Targets 160-6 t3 + 52216 t4.
  5. "Read with data_only=True; never drop a formula/non-numeric cell from an aggregate." Targets 374-9 (0.13).
  6. "Populate every target cell with its computed value; don't trust a leftover pre-existing formula (stale on hidden data)." Targets 52216 t4 (0.67, test 3). Formula-NEUTRAL wording.
  7. "'including the subsequent N periods' = N+1 inclusive; read in-sheet footnotes defining ranges." Targets 32468 (0.00, 13- vs 12-month window).
- Expected effect + why safe: all 7 are additive KNOWLEDGE/contract; none loosens an ACT-vs-REFUSE or write-scope rule. Verified passing tasks unaffected: 418-29/40467/47484 already inspect first (2 rounds) and don't aggregate formula cells; 47484 emitted XML yet still passed (recovers), so removing the wasted round can't hurt; 40467 writes live formulas and rewrites all target cells → complies with rules 5/6 unchanged. Blast radius bounded by construction (each rule fires only on the failing condition class).
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 REJECTED (broke 418-29, fixed 160-6) — its whole batch reverted. I did NOT re-introduce its "preview mislabels the first data row as header / distrust pandas headers / read by coordinate" claim, which most plausibly broke 418-29 (whose winning code relies on `read_excel(header=None)`). I kept the seed's structure fully intact rather than rewriting.
- Refuted hypotheses (never re-test): "grader ignores/penalizes formulas → avoid formulas" is FALSE — 40467 passes 5/5 writing live formulas (grader recalcs). Do NOT add any anti-formula rule.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 55457 (0.00) = empty instruction, unfixable by prompt (skip permanently). 32468 window and 52216 selector-cell identification are partly domain-reasoning; rules 6/7 attempt them but may not fully land.
- Plateau signal: only 2 iterations so far. If this is rejected as net-zero/negative, the next lever is to trim to ONLY the two safest, highest-leverage edits (Rule 1 output-contract + Rule 5 data_only) and re-test in isolation, since bundling many prompt rules risks diluting the strong reader.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, push 374-9/52216 remaining variance (formula recomputation robustness) and re-examine 32468's window with a sharper general inclusive-range example; leave 55457 alone.
